From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@brightlane.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate uplift request — production launch traffic

Avery,

We're hitting a sudden burst on our new feature rollout and hitting the current quota within minutes. Attach is a small export of calls in the last 30 minutes. Can you advise on a minute-scale guard or a way to absorb traffic without immediate throttles?

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood enable a temporary minute-level rate ceiling for the next 12–24 hours so our frontend doesn't show errors?
- If we exceed our committed tier, what's the billing approach? We're open to a short-term uplift but need clarity on retro adjustments or smoothing — especially since this is launch traffic and not sustained.

We're on a tight timeline (traffic will be highest through tonight PST). If there is a procurement/PO path that moves fast, please point us there.

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform, BrightLane

Thanks for the heads up, Sarah — and congrats on the launch. We can help avoid frontend errors. Proposed operational plan below (I can make the changes immediately once we agree):

1) Minute-scale guard: we can open a short-lived rate ceiling that increases per-minute concurrency for the next 12 hours. This will keep the requests flowing while we monitor error rates.
2) Billing and retro treatment: our standard temporary uplift is billed at the overrun rate (per-token) by default. However, we can offer a smoothing concession that applies a capped retro credit if overrun exposure is limited and you commit to a 3-month minimum commitment for the next billing cycle.

I've attached a quick proposed-pricing-matrix showing (A) immediate uplift rate, (B) a 72-hour discounted overrun band, and (C) a cap where we would invoice the uplift but issue a retro credit up to the agreed threshold. Ben — cc'ing you to confirm discount flexibility and sign-off path.

If you approve, I'll request the minute-ceiling now and follow up with the internal paper trail for the concession.

— Avery

Sarah — happy to help. Operationally we can:
- Authorize a minute-scale ceiling for 12–24 hours right away.
- Offer a promotional discount on overrun billing for the first 72 hours of the event (20% off the overrun rate) if BrightLane signs a short amendment committing to a 3-month incremental minimum (simple addendum to your existing contract).

Sarah — following up with final operational and commercial confirmation.

Operationally:
- We've enabled the minute-scale ceiling (effective now) for 24 hours and will monitor metrics. Engineering will rollback the temporary guard if error rates look anomalous.

Commercially (exception approval):
- Temporary uplift will be billed at the overrun rate shown in the matrix.
- Redwood will apply a 15% retro credit on overrun charges for the first 72 hours of this event, capped at $12,000, provided BrightLane signs an addendum for a 3-month incremental commitment by end of next billing period.
- If BrightLane's uplift exceeds the cap, standard overrun rates apply for the excess.

Attached is a brief SOW amendment (SOW-draft.pdf) and the DocuSign link to execute the addendum quickly. Once countersigned, finance will reflect the credit on the next invoice as a line item called "Launch Relief Credit."

Next steps:
1) Sarah — please confirm estimated token/request uplift so we can provision monitoring dashboards and estimate exposure.
2) If you accept the commercial terms above, sign the addendum via DocuSign and we'll finalize.

Onboarding contact for procurement flow: finance@brightlane.com (for PO) — if you prefer, we can accept a PO number and invoice on Net 30 as usual.

Best,
